pois.name: Asmara: A Modernist African City
pois.blurb: Asmara ( əs-MAHR-ə), or Asmera, is the capital and most populous city of Eritrea, in the country's Central Region. It sits at an elevation of 2,325 metres (7,628 ft), making it the sixth-highest capital in the world by altitude and the second-highest capital in Africa.

theme.title: UNESCO World Heritage Sites Inside National Capitals
theme.introduction: A daily location theme built around officially designated UNESCO World Heritage properties, or their separately named components, that physically lie within the present-day municipal boundaries of a country’s current national capital. Plausible locations include: Historic Centre of Rome; Vatican City; Paris, Banks of the Seine; Grand-Place, Brussels; Historic Centre of Vienna; Historic Centre of Prague; Historic Centre of Warsaw; Historic Centre of Tallinn; Historic Centre of Riga; Vilnius Historic Centre; City of Valletta; Budapest, including the Banks of the Danube and Buda Castle Quarter; Walled City of Baku; Boyana Church, Sofia; Moscow Kremlin and Red Square; Church of the Ascension at Kolomenskoye, Moscow; Saint-Sophia Cathedral and Related Monastic Buildings, Kyiv; Kyiv-Pechersk Lavra; Suomenlinna, Helsinki; Old City of Bern; Old Quarters and Fortifications of Luxembourg City; Historic Centre of San Marino; Jerónimos Monastery and Belém Tower, Lisbon; Old Havana; Historic Centre of Mexico City; Luis Barragán House and Studio, Mexico City; City of Quito; Historic Centre of Lima; Brasília; Historic City of Sucre; Historic Inner City of Paramaribo; Colonial City of Santo Domingo; Historic Cairo; Rabat, Modern Capital and Historic City; Medina of Tunis; Kasbah of Algiers; Asmara: A Modernist African City; Hanoi’s Central Sector of the Imperial Citadel of Thang Long; Imperial Palace and Historic Centre of Beijing; Temple of Heaven, Beijing; Summer Palace, Beijing; Kathmandu Durbar Square; Swayambhunath, Kathmandu; Singapore Botanic Gardens; Changdeokgung Palace Complex, Seoul; Jongmyo Shrine, Seoul; and San Agustin Church, Manila.
theme.inclusionCriteria: Include only a location that satisfies all of these conditions: (1) it is an individually named UNESCO World Heritage property or an individually named component of a UNESCO World Heritage property; (2) the property or component is physically located within the current municipal boundaries of a present-day national capital city; (3) its UNESCO World Heritage inscription is active, not merely proposed or tentative; and (4) the exact site can be identified on a map as a visitable landmark, complex, district, building, garden, or archaeological area. The country’s constitutional, executive, or de facto capital may qualify only if it is the officially recognized current national capital at the time of play.
